span.label: method
span.quote: Results suggest that the representation of mathematical problems as a strategy is an evidence-based practice based on the criteria set by Gersten et al.

span.label: mathematical problem representation instruction
span.quote: The purpose of the present review was to evaluate the quality of the research and evidence base for representation of problems as a strategy to enhance the mathematical performance of students with learning disabilities and those at risk for mathematics difficulties.

span.label: systematic-review
span.quote: The authors evaluated 25 experimental and quasiexperimental studies according to the Gersten et al. (2005) guidelines for group research studies.

span.label: some methodological quality components were unmet across the reviewed studies, to be addressed by future research
span.note: what this limits: the strength of the review's conclusions: FUTURE RESEARCHERS [must] ADDRESS THE COMPONENTS THAT DID NOT MEET THE MINIMUM REQUIREMENTS OR WERE FREQUENTLY UNMET
span.quote: Although these findings are encouraging, it is important for future researchers to address the components that did not met the minimum requirements or were frequently unmet in this database.

span.label: Representations were bundled into multicomponent interventions, so their independent contribution cannot be isolated.
span.note: what this limits: any claim about representations specifically: THE MAJORITY OF STUDIES INCLUDED REPRESENTATIONS AS PART OF MULTICOMPONENT INTERVENTIONS, MAKING IT DIFFICULT TO DETERMINE THE INFLUENCE OF REPRESENTATI[ons]
span.quote: A caveat to the findings is that the majority of studies included representations as part of multicomponent interventions, making it difficult to determine the influence of representations per se.

span.label: Which intervention element drove the outcomes is unknown because elements varied across studies.
span.note: what this limits: any attribution of the outcome to a particular element: IT IS NOT CLEAR WHICH ELEMENT OR COMBINATION OF ELEMENTS WAS RELATED TO THE OUTCOME
span.quote: The specific elements in the interventions that included representations varied across studies, and it is not clear which element or combination of elements was related to the outcome.

span.label: The conditions under which the practice works were not established.
span.note: what this limits: any implementation guidance: THE CONDITIONS UNDER WHICH THE PRACTICE OF REPRESENTING PROBLEMS IS EFFECTIVE WAS ALSO NOT CLEAR
span.quote: The conditions under which the practice of representing problems is effective was also not clear.

span.label: schema-based instruction and mathematical representations grounded in cognitive-load theory, applied to teaching students with learning difficulties
span.quote: in the literature on cognitive load theory

span.label: a fixed 25th-percentile cutoff for at-risk status, with studies using a higher cutoff excluded and mixed samples required to disaggregate or be majority LD/at-risk
span.note: eliminates: that the pooled effect is diluted by studies counting higher-attaining children as at risk - the cutoff is fixed to the published convention rather than to what each study chose
span.quote: We excluded studies that used a cutoff higher than the 25th percentile to identify students at risk for MD.

span.label: quality indicators
span.quote: The focus of our review was to evaluate the body of research on representation of problems as a strategy for students with MD by applying the quality indicators and standards for evidence-based practices proposed by Gersten et al

span.label: evidence-based practices
span.quote: The focus of our review was to evaluate the body of research on representation of problems as a strategy for students with MD by applying the quality indicators and standards for evidence-based practices proposed by Gersten et al

span.label: representation
span.quote: Results suggest that the representation of mathematical problems as a strategy is an evidence-based practice based on the criteria set by Gersten et al

span.label: A LITERATURE GRADED AGAINST A PUBLISHED CHECKLIST, AND THE ATTRITION IS ITEMISED RATHER THAN SCORED. 25 studies reviewed; `Thirteen of the 25 studies provided strong evidence of rigorous research across the four categories of the essential QIs`; and `ONLY EIGHT of the 13 studies that met the essential QIs provided evidence of meeting AT LEAST FOUR DESIRABLE INDICATORS to be classified as high quality.` **25 to 13 to 8**, with each drop attributable to a named criterion rather than to a composite score. That is the `tool must be checkable` principle applied to a whole field: external criteria, per-criterion grading, failures named
span.quote: Only eight of the 13 studies that met the essential QIs provided evidence of meeting at least four desirable indicators to be classified as high quality

span.label: AND THE MISSING INDICATORS ARE NAMED ONE BY ONE, WHICH IS WHAT MAKES THE REVIEW ACTIONABLE: one study `failed to provide sufficient information on teachers delivering the intervention`; of the eight high-quality studies `ONLY FIVE ... also documented that data collectors were BLIND TO CONDITIONS`; only one `provided information on the QUALITY OF IMPLEMENTATION`; and **`NONE OF THE STUDIES used excerpts from audio or videotape recordings to summarize the nature of the intervention`** - a zero across all 25. A reviewer reading this knows exactly what the next study should add, which a quality SCORE would not have told them
span.quote: None of the studies used excerpts from audio or videotape recordings to summarize the nature of the intervention

span.label: THE VERDICT IS EXPLICITLY RELATIVE TO ITS CRITERIA: `Results suggest that the representation of mathematical problems as a strategy is an EVIDENCE-BASED PRACTICE BASED ON THE CRITERIA SET BY GERSTEN ET AL.` **The qualifier is inside the claim.** `Evidence-based` is not asserted as a property of the practice but as the output of a named, published standard - so a reader who rejects the standard knows exactly what they are rejecting, and a different standard could give a different answer without either party being wrong about the studies
span.quote: Results suggest that the representation of mathematical problems as a strategy is an evidence-based practice based on the criteria set by Gersten et al

span.quote: Therefore, our review evaluated the quality of the research and evidence base for representation of problems as a strategy for students with MD using criteria for group research proposed by Gersten et al. (2005).

span.label: replicates → Gersten, Beckmann et al. (2009); Gersten, Chard et al. (2009)
span.quote: Further, the findings that the weighted mean effect sizes of +0.62 for students with LD, +0.70 for students at risk for MD, and +0.95 for both students with LD and those at risk for MD support the results of prior research about the benefits of representations for students struggling in mathematics (Gersten, Beckmann et al., 2009; Gersten, Chard et al., 2009).

span.label: quality indicators —operationalised-as→ evidence-based practices
span.note: strength of the relation: 0.9 — **THE `BY APPLYING` IS THE WHOLE EDGE AND IT IS IN THE QUOTE.** `Evidence-based practice` here is not a property discovered in the world but the output of applying a named checklist, and the paper says so in the sentence that makes the claim. Weight 0.9. This is the cleanest `operationalised-as` I have tagged: the construct and its operational definition are in one clause, and the definition is external and citable.
span.quote: The focus of our review was to evaluate the body of research on representation of problems as a strategy for students with MD by applying the quality indicators and standards for evidence-based practices proposed by Gersten et al

span.label: instructional approach (schema-based / visual representation)
span.note: retracted: RE-GROUNDED, AND THE REPLACEMENT USES DIFFERENT WORDS THAN THE TITLE ON PURPOSE. The evidence was a substring of the paper's own title, 'Schema-Based Instruction for Students with Learning Difficulties'. **The phrase `schema-based instruction` occurs ZERO times in the staged body**: `schema` appears 10 times, once as a diagram type in a list ('strip or tape, schema, percentage bar') and otherwise as `schematic representations`, never as the named approach the title advertises. So the variable is real and the paper discusses it under the word `schematic`; this span is the paper contrasting the two representation types the variable ranges over. A title naming a construct the body never names is also a truncation signal and is flagged as one. See Q-716.
span.quote: there is evidence that compared to pictorial (iconic) representations (focus on visual appearance of the objects described in a problem), schematic representations (focus on relevant data and relations in the problem) are more meaningful
